algorithm: Thread-pool work queue with a shared queue.Queue and sentinel shutdown

classes.desc: A unit of work with a numeric id, a kind label, and a payload string.
classes.name: Job

classes.desc: Thread-pool queue that runs Jobs on worker threads and records per-job results.
classes.name: TaskQueue

complexity: O(1) enqueue/dequeue; wall time scales with jobs/workers
data_flow_ascii:
jobs -> TaskQueue.submit -> queue.Queue
queue.Queue -> worker threads -> (job_id, digest, ms) rows
rows -> TaskQueue.results (sorted) -> printed table + stats
description_sentence: A multithreaded task queue that fans jobs out to a worker pool and reports per-job timing and result digests.
failure_note: Per-job exceptions are captured as ERROR digests so one bad job cannot kill a worker; shutdown uses sentinels for a clean join.

functions.desc: Enqueue a Job for the worker threads.
functions.name: TaskQueue.submit

functions.desc: Start workers, wait until the queue drains, then shut them down.
functions.name: TaskQueue.run

functions.desc: Completed (job_id, kind, worker, elapsed_ms, digest) rows sorted by job id.
functions.name: TaskQueue.results

functions.desc: Aggregate job count plus total and mean elapsed milliseconds.
functions.name: TaskQueue.stats

functions.desc: Build n demo Job objects with seeded random payloads.
functions.name: make_jobs
functions.signature: make_jobs(n: int, kinds: list, rng: random.Random) -> list

functions.desc: Build the command-line parser for the demo.
functions.name: build_parser

functions.desc: Submit demo jobs, run the queue, print the results table, return exit code.
functions.name: main

label: task queue
output_shape: Prints a per-job table (id, kind, worker, elapsed ms, digest) plus aggregate timing stats.
pitch_sentence: I built a {topic} that distributes work across a pool of threads and reports per-job results and timing.

qa.a: After the queue drains, run() pushes one None sentinel per worker; each worker exits when it pulls its sentinel.
qa.q: How do workers know when to stop?

qa.a: The worker catches it, records an ERROR digest for that job, and keeps processing the rest of the queue.
qa.q: What happens if one job raises an exception?

qa.a: Job payloads are seeded, but per-job elapsed times vary with machine load; the table layout and digests are stable.

resume_bullet_template: Built a {topic} in Python with worker threads and a shared queue, adding per-job timing and SHA-256 digest verification in the demo run.
run_notes: --workers, --jobs, and --kinds override the demo configuration from @@TOPIC_PARAMS@@.
scaling_note: Single process and GIL-bound; fine for dozens of workers on I/O or hashing-style work, not a substitute for a distributed queue.
storage_note: In-memory only: queued jobs and results live in process memory and are gone when the program exits.
tech_stack: stdlib: argparse, hashlib, queue, random, threading, time
tradeoff_note: Threads keep the code simple versus processes, at the cost of true parallelism for CPU-heavy jobs under the GIL.
